title: Ayyub's Oath
art: Ayyub appears only as a steady light; his wife and children as dim figures of light. His wealth, herds and family before the trial are told in the commentaries; the Quran names his trial, his prayer and his patience. His illness is never shown: his light only dims. His land is drawn as the wheat plains of the Hauran, where tradition places him; his farmhouse is imagined.

That Ayyub had sworn an oath in his illness (the commentators say about a word of his wife's) and that he kept it is from the traditions on 38:44; the wife, the number of his children and the bundle of grass are not counted or named on screen.
The bundle of grass is shown as the Quran describes it (38:44): a bunch taken in the hand. Only the bundle is shown, gathered and laid down; no one is hurt.
imagePrompt: The same wheat plain in the evening light, the black basalt farmhouse and the clear spring beside it; a bright steady light bending in the wheat and gathering a small bundle of grass in one hand; a dim amber light standing close beside him; then the bundle of grass laid down on the ground between them, and the two lights standing still together; ink-wash and parchment texture.

beats.say: In his long illness Ayyub had sworn an oath; the commentators say it was over a word of his wife's. Now he was healed, and he meant to keep his word.
God gave him a gentle way to keep it: to take a small bundle of grass in his hand. He kept his word, and no one was hurt.

verse.en: [We said], "And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath."
